roadmap.goal: ADO User Story #5884. A flow coach opening either Work Item Age dialog reads, on every in-flight row, which pace band that item's age falls into for the state it is in — the same judgement the chart already paints as a coloured zone under the same dot — and can then order the list worst-band-first, cut it to one band, and carry it out as a CSV whose band column reads in words. Two slices: slice 01 (US-01 + US-02) makes the column exist and be right; slice 02 (US-03) makes the list orderable, filterable and exportable. Zero backend change, zero migration, zero new dependency (DDD-10). DISTILL has ALREADY authored all 77 Vitest acceptance tests; they sit on disk behind `describe.skip`. DELIVER authors no Vitest test: every step un-skips a named group, watches it go red for the right reason, implements until green, and commits. The one exception is 02-02, the Playwright skeleton DT-9 deliberately assigned here so it could be written and RUN together.

validation.notes: Nine steps over two slices for roughly two days of frontend work, split along the DISTILL handoff's own sequence. Seven production files, so the decomposition ratio is 9/7 = 1.29, inside the 2.5 bar. `files_to_modify` deliberately lists production files only: the sole permitted diff to any of the four Vitest acceptance files is a `.skip` marker, and each is already named in its step's `test_file`. A reviewer should check three things in particular: (a) that no step's criteria could be met by weakening an assertion — DELIVER does not own these tests; (b) that the interim-red windows are handled by commit-without-push rather than by re-skipping a group already un-skipped; (c) whether the two deviations recorded in `maintainer_decisions` are accepted as written. The five criteria on each step are the reviewer's done-check; the standing guards that apply to every step — the shipped-test survival gate, `pnpm build` clean, Biome clean, no assertion edits, no file outside `files_to_modify` — live at the head of each step's `implementation_notes` and are passed to the crafter verbatim.

maintainer_decisions: The step sequence is DISTILL's handoff sequence (feature-delta.md:952-975), not a new decomposition. Its eight items map onto these nine steps in the same order: handoff 1 folds into 01-01, handoff 2 becomes 01-01/01-02/01-03, handoff 3 becomes 01-04, handoff 4 becomes 01-05, handoff 5 becomes 01-06, handoff 6 becomes 01-07, handoff 7 becomes 02-01, handoff 8 becomes 02-02. Nothing is reordered.

DEVIATION 1 — handoff item 2 is split into three steps. As written it un-skips all 46 tests of paceBands.test.ts in one go, which is a batch far past the sizing bar. The file's five inner describes make the cut obvious and cost nothing: un-skip the OUTER describe once, at 01-01, and leave the not-yet-implemented inner describes carrying their own `.skip` until their step reaches them. The three steps are ladder resolution (01-01), classification (01-02), and naming/colouring/packaging (01-03). No test is reordered, renamed or moved.

DEVIATION 2 — 02-02's two files, `Lighthouse.EndToEndTests/tests/specs/flow/AgingPacePercentiles.spec.ts` and `Lighthouse.EndToEndTests/tests/models/metrics/WorkItemAgingChart.ts`, are NOT rows in the DESIGN component decomposition table. They are named by DISTILL DT-9, which deliberately deferred the single Playwright walking skeleton out of DISTILL into DELIVER slice 02 so it could be written and RUN in the same step. This is a pre-authorised addition recorded upstream, not a design deviation discovered by a crafter. Every other step's files_to_modify is a row of the DESIGN table.

The palette collapse is the FIRST act of the FIRST step and gets its own commit inside it. DT-5 shipped `PACE_BAND_COLORS_LOW_TO_HIGH` declared twice on purpose — once in the new pure module, once still in the chart — as the cheapest honest scaffold state, and said DELIVER collapses it first. Two identical five-entry arrays must not survive into a second step, let alone to the end of the wave.

There is no standalone type-level-compile step, and that is deliberate. DESIGN's open question 2 made `pnpm build` with the widened `DataGridColumn` and a live `singleSelect` column the first act of slice 01; DT-3 discharged it during DISTILL by compiling a probe (made to fail on purpose first, then deleted) and the widening is already committed. Re-proving it as a step would produce a step with an empty files_to_modify that only runs a validator. The obligation is instead carried in the notes of 01-01, and again of 02-01, which is the step that first puts a live `singleSelect` + `valueOptions` column through `DataGridBase`'s checked initializer. If 02-01's build fails, STOP — the remedy (a cast at the initializer, or threading getOptionLabel/getOptionValue through a shared component) is larger than DDD-6 promises and is a design escalation, not a crafter decision.

NO Vitest test-authoring step, and exactly one Playwright-authoring step (02-02, assigned here by DT-9). DISTILL authored all 77 Vitest scenarios and ran the fail-for-the-right-reason gate, catching and fixing one vacuous pass. Per ADR-025 / the slim-crafter scope, DELIVER implements against tests it does not own. The ONLY permitted edit to any of the four Vitest acceptance files is removing or adding a `.skip` marker — which is why those files appear in each step's `test_file` and NOT in its `files_to_modify`. If a test looks wrong, STOP and raise it; do not adjust it.

Interim red is accepted, bounded, and never pushed. Slice 01 leaves later groups skipped rather than red, so `pnpm test` is green at the end of every step except the moment a group is un-skipped. Per the project's green-before-push rule, commit at every step and push at slice boundaries once CI-parity gates are green. `pnpm build` and Biome are gated at EVERY step; they do not depend on the test suite.

The 22 existing pace-band tests in WorkItemAgingChart.test.tsx (16 direct unit tests of computePaceBandRects plus 6 overlay DOM tests in the same describe, and two further DOM tests elsewhere in the file) are a PER-STEP gate, not an end-of-slice one. They are the instrument that makes the DDD-1 extraction a bounded risk; a step that leaves any of them red has broken the shipped overlay and must not be committed.

Definition of Done items 10 and 11 — timing Paul Brown's current-path shortlist baseline before he sees the column, and securing his commitment to record the flipside-table verdict on ADO #5884 — are human tasks with no crafter surface. They are deliberately absent from this roadmap and are tracked by the orchestrator.

Stryker mutation testing is the project's per-feature gate and belongs after 02-02, at feature finalization, not to any step here. Both stacks' 80% kill rate applies to the frontend changes only; there are no backend mutations to run because there are no backend changes.

KNOWN GAP, raised not papered over: nothing in the authored suite exercises `buildViewData` constructing the descriptor. The two WidgetShell tests mock the dialog and assert only that the shell forwards, so the View Data route can be fully green in Vitest while the descriptor never reaches a real dialog. 01-06 carries a dogfood criterion as the compensating check pending the maintainer's decision on whether this goes back to DISTILL for a scenario or rides on the 02-02 walking skeleton.
out_of_scope: Every backend file. Zero C#, zero endpoint, zero DTO field, zero EF migration, zero schema change, zero cache key, zero premium gate, zero new runtime dependency (DDD-10). Both `ageInStatePercentiles` routes are consumed exactly as they ship today. A step that finds itself opening `Lighthouse.Backend/` has misread the feature.

`Lighthouse.Frontend/src/components/Common/DataGrid/types.ts`. Its one optional `valueOptions?: string[]` is already committed as the DT-3 scaffold and proven to compile. No step re-opens it. If one needs to, that is a design escalation.

Any production file outside the six the DESIGN component decomposition table names, plus the two E2E files DT-9 names. `DataGridBase.tsx`, `DataGridToolbar.tsx`, `useDataGridExport`, `getColumnColor`, `hexToRgba`, `useTerminology`, `useShowPaceBands`, `IPerStatePercentileValues` are all REUSE AS-IS in the Reuse Analysis. Needing a ninth file means STOP and report.

Changing what export writes. DDD-13 is settled: the file carries the dialog's whole row set in sort order, not the filtered rows. `useDataGridExport`'s `visibleRows` variable and the comment above it still claim filters apply and still do not — that is a pre-existing product-wide behaviour recorded in design/upstream-changes.md, and #5884 is not the change that carries the fix. A one-line selector swap here would quietly change what every grid in the product writes to disk.

Any `exportTable` on this dialog (DDD-15). The band's `valueGetter` returns the label, so `getCellValue` is already correct; adding `exportTable` here would make this one call site own export formatting for all sixteen render sites, and would silently bypass the valueGetter.

Persisting the filter model. `PersistedGridState.filterModel` is declared and nothing reads or writes it; `DataGridBase` passes neither `filterModel` nor `onFilterModelChange`. No acceptance criterion depends on a filter surviving a dialog close, and building the persistence is explicitly not recommended.

Bumping the `work-items-dialog` storage key, or teaching `DataGridBase` to insert a new column at its declared index. DDD-14 accepts that a returning user with a persisted column order gets the band appended last, past Time in State; Reset Layout restores the declared position. Both alternatives would damage sixteen dialogs, or every grid in the product, to move one column.

Multi-band filter selection, a toolbar filter button, and any chip row or bespoke filter control (D3). `singleSelect` filters one value at a time; whether reviews want two bands at once is what slice 02's learning hypothesis exists to answer.

Any other widget's View Data dialog, including `ItemsInProgress.tsx` (D6). The `ageBandColumn` prop is optional and absent by default, so none of the other call sites is edited or behaves differently (D17).
Colouring the age column beside the band, changing either dialog's default sort, widening the dot-click dialog's population (D1), and any per-cell caveat on the last Doing state (D10).

Editing, adding to, weakening or reordering any assertion in the four Vitest acceptance files. Removing and adding `.skip` is the only permitted edit there, which is why those files are named in `test_file` and never in `files_to_modify`.

Docs, the docs page, `@screenshot` regeneration and website copy. Per the project's per-feature-not-batched rule these land at feature finalization, after 02-02 — and, per the standing feedback, after the maintainer has confirmed the behaviour in their own environment.

A second E2E spec, or any E2E permutation by owner. One walking skeleton, extending the existing spec through its existing page object (E2E minimalism). The portfolio twin of the aging-pace spec was deliberately deleted once already; do not reintroduce its shape.
Definition of Done items 10 and 11 — the timed shortlist baseline and Paul Brown's recorded verdict. Human tasks, tracked by the orchestrator.

steps.name: Collapse the duplicate palette and resolve the ladders
criteria: The pace-band palette is declared in exactly one place; the chart re-exports it and no existing importer or test needed an edit
A state reads against its own percentiles in value-ascending order, whatever order those percentiles arrived in
A state without finished history of its own reads against the nearest populated state before it in the workflow
A state with nothing before it to inherit is absent from the ladders entirely, rather than present and empty

steps.scenario_name: describe("resolving the ladders across the workflow") — gives a state its own percentiles in value-ascending order | lets a state with no finished history of its own read against the state before it | leaves a state with nothing before it to inherit out of the ladders entirely | reads percentiles in whatever order they arrive | ignores a state whose percentile list came back empty | produces no ladders at all for a team with no finished history anywhere | produces no ladders when the workflow itself is empty | carries a single-percentile history forward just as it carries a full one | answers the same way however many times it is asked
steps.implementation_notes:
WHAT THIS STEP DOES — two commits, in this order.

COMMIT 1, the palette collapse and nothing else. `PACE_BAND_COLORS_LOW_TO_HIGH` is currently declared twice: in the new `utils/charts/paceBands.ts` (the DT-5 scaffold) and still in `WorkItemAgingChart.tsx:60`. Delete the chart's copy and re-export the module's, so existing importers and tests are untouched. Do the same for the position-clamp helper at `WorkItemAgingChart.tsx:86` if it moves cleanly; if it does not, leave it and take it in 01-04, but the palette itself moves now. Run `pnpm test src/components/Common/Charts/WorkItemAgingChart.test.tsx` and confirm all 22 existing pace-band tests are still green BEFORE committing.

COMMIT 2, un-skip and implement. Change `describe.skip("pace band ladder")` at `paceBands.test.ts:78` to `describe(...)`, and add `.skip` to the four inner describes this step does not cover: `"placing an age against a state's ladder"` (:167), `"naming the band"` (:239), `"colouring the band"` (:294), `"the column descriptor handed to the work item dialog"` (:313). Watch the nine tests of `"resolving the ladders across the workflow"` go red naming `resolvePaceBandLadders` — the scaffold body throws a message naming itself, so a red naming anything else is a wiring problem, not a missing contract. Then replace that body: `resolvePaceBandLadders({ perStatePercentileValues, doingStates })` returns the ladders keyed by workflow position, each carrying the state name and its value-ascending percentile list after carry-forward.

FILE ROLES — `paceBands.ts`: replace the `resolvePaceBandLadders` scaffold body, keep every other body throwing. `WorkItemAgingChart.tsx`: delete the duplicate palette, re-export the module's.

STANDING GUARDS, all of them gates on this step even though they are not in the five criteria: all 22 shipped pace-band tests in `WorkItemAgingChart.test.tsx` green after the palette commit AND at the end of the step; a single-percentile history carries forward exactly as a full one does; asking twice returns the same answer, because the resolver mutates none of its inputs; `pnpm build` zero errors and zero warnings with the already-committed `DataGridColumn.valueOptions` widening in place, whose prebuild hook implies a clean Biome check on ./src; no assertion in `paceBands.test.ts` added, edited, widened or weakened — the ONLY diff to that file is `.skip` markers; no file outside the two in `files_to_modify` touched.

THE PALETTE MUST NOT SURVIVE THIS STEP IN TWO PLACES. DT-5 shipped it twice deliberately, as the cheapest honest scaffold state — the alternative was making a pure module import a component — and named DELIVER's first act as the collapse. A wave that closes with two identical five-entry arrays has quietly re-created the drift ADR-188 exists to forbid.

The module is pure and React-free and imports NOTHING from `components/`. That is fork 2's structural enforcement layer: this repo has no ArchUnit for TypeScript, so the module boundary, the shared ladder type and the 01-04 agreement property are the whole honest enforcement set. An import from `components/` here reverses the dependency the moment the chart changes.

Carry-forward is workflow-ORDER-driven, not alphabetical and not input-order-driven: `doingStates` is the order. Case-insensitivity is on the state NAME match only. Both rules are already in `computePaceBandRects` (`WorkItemAgingChart.tsx:92-163`); read them there rather than re-deriving them.

`Array.prototype.at` is NOT available under this project's `es2021` target — DISTILL hit this twice while writing the tests. Index from `length - 1`.

CI learnings apply (docs/ci-learnings.md — consult before writing, per CLAUDE.md). No new SonarQube issue of any severity; if a rule genuinely conflicts with a deliberate choice, suppress narrowly at the call site with a plain-language justification.

EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: this step authors no tests — DISTILL owns the acceptance suite and the slim-crafter scope forbids widening it — so the Hypothesis/state-delta unit mandate has no surface here. The compensating rigour is DISTILL's own: 46 unit scenarios over this module alone, including two explicitly property-shaped ones ("reads percentiles in whatever order they arrive", "answers the same way however many times it is asked"), all past a fail-for-the-right-reason gate.

steps.name: Place an age against a state's ladder
criteria: Thirteen walked ages in Review each land in the rank their ladder names, every boundary hit exactly and on both sides
An age sitting exactly on a percentile value falls in the band beneath it, never above
A state name differing from the percentile data only in capitalisation is still recognised
An age in a state without history of its own is placed against the ladder it inherited
A state with nothing to measure against, or absent from the workflow, yields no answer rather than a default rank
steps.scenario_name: describe("placing an age against a state's ladder") — places {7,8,9,11,12,13,16,17,18,23,24,25,260} days in Review at the rank its ladder names (it.each, 13 cases) | places an age at the very floor in the lowest band | recognises a state whose name differs only in capitalisation | places an age against the inherited ladder when the state has no history of its own | has no answer for a state with nothing to measure against | has no answer for a state that is not part of the workflow | never lands on a band that two identical boundaries have collapsed to nothing
steps.implementation_notes:
WHAT THIS STEP DOES — remove the `.skip` from `describe("placing an age against a state's ladder")` at `paceBands.test.ts:167`. Nineteen tests go red naming `classifyPaceBand`, thirteen of them one `it.each` walking {7,8,9,11,12,13,16,17,18,23,24,25,260} days in Review across that state's four boundaries. Implement `classifyPaceBand(ageInDays, stateName, ladders)`: it returns the rank of the first boundary the age does not exceed, or the top rank when it exceeds all of them, and returns nothing when the state has no ladder or is not part of the workflow order. That single comparison IS the half-open `(lower, upper]` rule — it is not a second statement of it. An age equal to a percentile lands in the band beneath, in this consumer and in the geometry, because there is only one comparison in the codebase to get right.

FILE ROLE — `paceBands.ts`: replace the `classifyPaceBand` scaffold body.

STANDING GUARDS, gates on this step: an age at the very floor lands in the lowest band; a classification NEVER lands on a band that two identical boundaries have collapsed to nothing; the nine tests greened by 01-01 stay green; all 22 shipped pace-band tests in `WorkItemAgingChart.test.tsx` stay green; `pnpm build` zero errors and zero warnings, Biome clean; no assertion in `paceBands.test.ts` added, edited, widened or weakened — the only diff is the `.skip` marker; no file outside `paceBands.ts` touched.

THE COLLAPSED-BAND CASE IS AN INVARIANT, NOT A GUARD YOU ADD. A band collapses only when two consecutive boundaries are equal, and selecting the FIRST boundary an age does not exceed always picks the lower, surviving one. If the implementation needs an explicit "skip zero-width bands" branch, the selection is wrong — go back to the single comparison. This is the same tie-break 01-04's agreement property relies on, and the reason a classification can never name a rect the geometry dropped.

`classifyPaceBand` returns a RANK, not a label and not a colour. Keeping those three separate is what lets DDD-2's derived labels and DDD-3's clamped colours change independently, and it is what makes DDD-5's comparator binding structural in 02-01.

Absence must be a real absence — a state with no ladder yields nothing, not rank 0 and not -1. Rank -1 is a SORT position that belongs to the option list in 02-01, and conflating the two here would put an unmeasurable item in the lowest coloured band.

The classifier takes no axis minimum or maximum and must not acquire one. ADR-188 states the bound explicitly: the geometry has the axis domain and the classifier does not, so what holds is that for an age inside the domain the two name the same rank. Outside it, the classifier is right and the chart's clipping is the artefact — a band is a property of the item and the ladder, not of the viewport.

EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: no tests are authored in this step. The compensating rigour is the boundary walk DISTILL already wrote — every partition boundary of a four-boundary ladder hit exactly and on both sides, plus the floor and a 260-day outlier.

criteria: Ranks 0 to 4 read Below 50th, 50th-70th, 70th-85th, 85th-95th, Above 95th; an absent rank reads No history
A short ladder's top band is named for the highest percentile it actually has, and painted the most alarming colour
The option list runs No history first and the worst band last, and the names use plain hyphens
The descriptor names the band beneath for an item exactly on a boundary, and leaves No history unpainted
buildAgeBandColumnDescriptor returns nothing at all when no state has any finished history
steps.scenario_name: describe("naming the band") — names rank {0..4} as {Below 50th … Above 95th} (it.each, 5 cases) | names an absent rank as no history | names the top band of a short ladder for the highest percentile it actually has | writes the band names with plain hyphens so they survive a spreadsheet unchanged | offers every band a team can show, no history first and the worst band last ‖ describe("colouring the band") — runs from the calmest colour at the floor to the alarming one at the top | still paints the worst band of a short ladder the most alarming colour | stops distinguishing colours past the palette and leaves the naming to carry it ‖ describe("the column descriptor handed to the work item dialog") — carries the header and the explanation it was given | names the band for an item that has run past every finished item before it | names the band for an item sitting exactly on a boundary as the band beneath | says no history for an item in a state nothing finished has left | gives every band the chart's own colour and leaves no history unpainted | offers nothing at all when no state has any finished history
steps.implementation_notes:
WHAT THIS STEP DOES — remove the `.skip` from the three remaining inner describes in `paceBands.test.ts`: `"naming the band"` (:239), `"colouring the band"` (:294) and `"the column descriptor handed to the work item dialog"` (:313). Eighteen tests go red naming `paceBandLabelForRank`, `paceBandOptionLabels`, `paceBandColorForRank` and `buildAgeBandColumnDescriptor`.

LABELS (DDD-2): derive the label from the boundary's percentile NUMBER — rank 0 is `Below {p0}th`, a middle rank is `{p(i-1)}th-{pi}th`, the top rank is `Above {plast}th`, an absent rank is the `No history` sentinel. On the shipped fixed 50/70/85/95 ladder this yields exactly D7's six strings.

COLOURS (DDD-3): `paceBandColorForRank(rank, boundaryCount)` carries the top-rank clamp the chart already applies — the top slice is painted reddest even when the ladder is short. `No history` gets no colour at all.

OPTIONS: `paceBandOptionLabels` returns the ordered list a team can actually show, `No history` first and the worst band last. This list is the one 02-01 uses as both `valueOptions` and the sort key.

FACTORY: `buildAgeBandColumnDescriptor({ perStatePercentileValues, doingStates, headerName, description })` returns `{ headerName, description, optionLabels, bandFor, colorForBand }`, or nothing at all when no state has a non-empty percentile list.

FILE ROLE — `paceBands.ts`: replace the `paceBandLabelForRank`, `paceBandOptionLabels`, `paceBandColorForRank` and `buildAgeBandColumnDescriptor` scaffold bodies. After this step no throwing body remains in the module.

STANDING GUARDS, gates on this step: the colours run from the calmest at the floor to the alarming one at the top; past the palette the colours stop distinguishing ranks and the naming carries the difference, which is existing chart behaviour kept rather than corrected; the descriptor carries the header and the explanation it was given; every test in `paceBands.test.ts` green — 46 of 46, no `.skip` left in the file; all 22 shipped pace-band tests stay green; `pnpm build` zero errors and zero warnings, Biome clean; no assertion added, edited, widened or weakened; no file outside `paceBands.ts` touched.

DERIVE THE LABEL FROM THE PERCENTILE NUMBER; DO NOT INDEX A FIXED ARRAY. DDD-2 is explicit that the honest reason is not that ladder lengths vary today — they do not, both metrics services hard-code [50, 70, 85, 95]. The derivation is written for the change already named and already deferred, configurable percentiles, under which a positional five-entry array would relabel a three-boundary ladder's top band `70th-85th` when it means `Above 85th`, silently, while the derivation needs no edit at all. A five-entry array passes every test in this file and is still the wrong answer.

PLAIN HYPHENS, NOT EN DASHES. `50th-70th` with U+002D. An en dash reads correctly on screen and mangles in a spreadsheet, which is the whole point of the test that pins it.

THE TOP-RANK CLAMP IS EXISTING CHART BEHAVIOUR, COPIED NOT CORRECTED. Past five ranks the colour deliberately stops following the label: a six-boundary ladder would show `85th-95th`, `95th-99th` and `Above 99th` in three identically coloured cells. DDD-3 keeps that rather than fixing it here.

The descriptor's `colorForBand` takes a LABEL and returns a colour or nothing. The dialog does not call `paceBandColorForRank` itself — the closure inside the descriptor does. That is what keeps `WorkItemsDialog` ignorant of ranks, percentiles and Doing states (DDD-4), and it is the shape the WidgetShell and dialog fixtures already assume.

Omission is the CALLER's decision, computed here inside the factory and nowhere else (DDD-9). The predicate is the same one the geometry applies: at least one state with a non-empty percentile list.

EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: no tests are authored in this step. The compensating rigour is the short-ladder and past-the-palette cases DISTILL wrote, which are precisely the two the fixed-array shortcut would pass on today's data and fail on tomorrow's.

This dialog deliberately takes the other route from its Time in State sibling: the `valueGetter` returns the label, `getCellValue` is already correct, and adding `exportTable` here would make this one call site own export formatting for all sixteen render sites AND would bypass the valueGetter, dropping the label from the file while the sort still passed.
